title: Macaron-V1: Mixture-of-LoRA for Continual Learning
hook: Freeze the base model, keep a shelf of specialist LoRA adapters, pick one per user turn. It's a bet that continual learning belongs in the adapters, not the weights.
key_points: Macaron-V1 is an open agent-model family built around learning from experience and continuing to learn after deployment.
Mixture-of-LoRA (MoL) freezes the base model, composes specialist LoRA adapters, and selects one LoRA per user turn.
The flagship Macaron-V1-Venti pairs a 744B GLM-5.2 base with four LoRAs — chat, agent, coding, and GenUI.
Macaron-V1-Tall (50B, Qwen3.6-based) applies the same design for local deployment.
Adaptation works by recursive improvement of versioned model-harness pairs: experience from one configuration is scored against an external contract and used to build its successor.
The authors state that compounding gains from continual learning remain an open question, not a demonstrated result.
content_html: Macaron-V1 is an open agent-model family organized around a single question: how does a model keep learning after it ships? Mind Lab's answer separates the problem into adaptation and collaboration, and puts a distinctive architecture underneath.
extra_html:
The architecture is Mixture-of-LoRA. Rather than routing tokens through experts inside every layer the way a standard MoE does, MoL freezes the base model, keeps a set of specialist LoRA adapters, and selects one per user turn. The flagship Macaron-V1-Venti combines a 744B GLM-5.2 base with four LoRAs covering chat, agent, coding, and GenUI; Macaron-V1-Tall uses the same design on a 50B Qwen3.6 base for local deployment. Because the base never moves, adding a capability means adding a specialist — which is exactly the property continual learning wants.

Adaptation is handled by recursive improvement over versioned model-harness pairs: experience from one configuration is evaluated under an external contract, and that evaluation constructs the successor. The report spans architecture, algorithms (the MindForge agentic RL framework, the LongStraw long-context RL method) and infrastructure. Notably, the authors close by saying the compounding gains from continual learning remain an open question rather than a demonstrated result. Mind Lab, August 2026.

related.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation
related.hook: Why retrain billions of weights when you can freeze them all and train tiny add-on matrices instead? LoRA tunes under ~1% of the parameters with near-full-fine-tune quality.

related.title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning (Adapters)
related.hook: Don't fine-tune the whole model for every new task — slip in a few tiny trainable modules and freeze the rest. This 2019 idea seeded parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

flashcards.prompt: How does Mixture-of-LoRA differ from a standard Mixture-of-Experts layer?

choices.text: It freezes the base model and selects one specialist LoRA adapter per user turn, rather than routing tokens through experts inside each layer
It routes each token to several LoRA adapters and averages their outputs
It merges all LoRA adapters into the base weights before inference

flashcards.explanation_html: MoL routes at the conversational-turn level over adapters, which is what makes it extensible — you can add a specialist without retraining the frozen base.

flashcards.prompt: What makes Mixture-of-LoRA a natural fit for continual learning?
flashcards.back_html: The base stays frozen, so new capabilities arrive as additional LoRA specialists rather than as edits to shared weights — extending the model without disturbing what it already does.

flashcards.prompt: How does Macaron-V1 produce each successive version of itself?
flashcards.back_html: Through recursive improvement of versioned model-harness pairs: experience gathered under one configuration is evaluated against an external contract, and that evaluation is used to construct the next version.
